brief: UBS CIO reads last Thursday's ~4% S&P 500 drop as positioning-driven, not fundamental: no major catalyst that day, but heavy retail, levered-ETF and systematic selling, while credit spreads barely widened (a 4% drop should move them near 10bps) and the VIX rose 70%, more than its usual S&P relationship implies, suggesting downside-protection buying that could extend the selloff. On the midterms: Democrats may rescind 2027 One Big Beautiful Bill spending cuts, adding ~20bps to GDP growth if successful; Trump keeps discretion on trade, regulation and foreign policy; and new Democratic governors in Texas, Georgia and Michigan, holding ~45% of planned US data-center capacity (Texas ~25% alone), could slow the AI buildout. UBS says the goal is self-reliance on power/grid/water, not a halt, so the hit is marginal and falls mainly on 2028-2029 since 2027 spend is committed; bigger AI-investment risk lies in energy, capital, chip or demand bottlenecks. October payrolls rose 165k with upward revisions (3-month average to 137k from 51k), supporting 2.5% Q4/Q4 2026 growth before 2% in 2027, so UBS expects another 25bp Fed hike in December and March. UBS calls the medium-term outlook positive but expects near-term volatility, and recommends using the selloff to add higher-quality exposure.

cards.claim: UBS attributes last Thursday's S&P 500 selloff more to positioning than to deteriorating fundamentals.
cards.anchor: Thursday’s sell-off appears to be due more to positioning than fundamentals.

cards.claim: Retail investor selling was unusually heavy on Thursday morning, selling in levered ETFs was also heavy, and systematic strategies increased selling through the day.
cards.anchor: retail investor selling was unusually heavy that morning, as was selling in levered ETFs, and systematic strategies increased selling as the day went on

cards.claim: Investment grade corporate bond spreads barely widened on Thursday, well below the roughly 10bps increase a 4% S&P 500 drop would typically imply.
cards.anchor: investment grade corporate bond spreads should have increased closer to 10bps based on a 4% drop in the S&P 500

cards.claim: The VIX rose 70% on Thursday, far more than its relationship to the S&P 500 over the prior six months would imply.
cards.anchor: the VIX index increased 70%, far more than would be implied by its relationship to the S&P 500 over the past six months.

cards.claim: UBS says the VIX move suggests investors were buying downside protection, which could amplify the move lower in equities.
cards.anchor: This suggests that investors were buying downside protection, which could amplify the move lower in equities.

cards.claim: Democrats in Congress will push to rescind One Big Beautiful Bill spending cuts set to begin in 2027, as part of funding the government and raising the debt ceiling.
